newsitem.title: JAPAN: FORECAST-Japan July-Sept GDP seen down 0.05 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Japan July-Sept GDP seen down 0.05 pct.

text.p: Japan's gross domestic product (GDP) for the July-September period is expected to fall by an average of 0.05 percent in real terms from the previous quarter, or an annualised fall of 0.2 percent, a Reuters poll of economists showed.

But opinion was split over whether Japan's economy would show marginal growth or shrink again from the previous quarter. In the April-June period, real GDP showed a quarter-on-quarter fall of 0.7 percent or an annualised drop of 2.9 percent.
The Economic Planning Agency will announce GDP data for the July-September quarter at 3.30 p.m. (0630 GMT) next Tuesday.
The forecasts for real GDP ranged from a fall of one percent to a rise of 0.3 percent, or an annualised fall of 3.8 percent to a rise of 1.2 percent.
"The key question is whether it (GDP) is going to be a negative number or a positive number," said ING Baring's Richard Jerram.
Economists see weak personal consumption and public works spending as the main factors limiting economic growth.
"Consumption has been weak in the third quarter...public works should be undergoing a wrenching slowdown," said BZW's Chris Calderwood.
The NLI Research Institute said the food poisoning epidemic which swept through Japan this summer and cool weather in September contributed to weak consumption.

Robert Feldman, chief economist at Salomon Brothers Asia, said he expects a recovery in the fourth quarter, compared with a lull in the previous quarter. "It (the recovery) is still on a moderate recovery track," said Feldman.
"Weak numbers will re-focus attention on debate over whether we need a stimulative supplementary budget," Feldman said.
